conversation.Statement: Hey there, Anna. Looks like the universe wanted us to reminisce together tonight.
Hi! That's a nice way to put it. I'm up for a little nostalgia therapy, honestly.
Perfect, because I'm convinced good memories are the secret ingredient to surviving adulthood. So, what's your happiest childhood memory?
Hmm... I'd say camping in the backyard with my sisters, making up silly ghost stories. It felt like such an adventure, even if we were only ten feet from the house.
That's adorable. I always wanted siblings for stuff like that. I mostly had to make up weird stories for my dog, who was a terrible audience.
Haha, at least dogs never judge your plot holes. Did your family camp a lot?

Not really. My parents ran a bakery, so weekends meant early mornings and dough everywhere. But we'd have midnight picnics in the kitchen. I still remember stealing fresh croissants off the cooling rack.
Now I'm jealous! Midnight pastries sound like heaven. Maybe that's why you're a food entrepreneur now?
Guilty as charged. I guess I'm just chasing that feeling of warmth and sneaky joy. There's something special about sharing food with people, you know?
Absolutely. I think that's why I love being a teacher, honestly. It's all about creating little moments for people to feel safe and seen.
That's beautiful. I noticed in your profile you teach high school, is it as wild as everyone says?
Some days are chaos, but I wouldn't trade it. Teenagers are hilarious and surprisingly honest. Plus, I get to relive all my awkward phases through them.
There's something magical about someone who can turn awkwardness into a superpower. I admire that. Must be hard, though, with your own kids off to college?
Yeah, it's been a tough adjustment. The house feels too quiet sometimes. I'm still figuring out how to fill the empty spaces.
I get that more than you know. My folks split up when I was little, and our house always felt a bit too big after. It's strange how silence can be louder than any noise.
You're right, it really can. I guess that's why I'm here, trying to make some new noise in my life.
Well, I'm honored to be part of the new soundtrack. And just so you know, you come across as incredibly genuine. It's refreshing.
Thank you... that means more than you think. It's hard not to feel invisible sometimes after a big life change.
If it's any comfort, I haven't stopped thinking about that spark of humor in your messages since we matched. You have a way of making even everyday stories sound special.
You really know how to make a girl blush. I appreciate that, seriously. I'm still learning how to accept compliments again.
All in good time. But for the record, I'm here for all the blushing and all the stories. You deserve to feel seen.
That's so sweet. So, if you could relive any childhood day, which would it be?
Easy. My ninth birthday, my dad let me decorate the bakery window. I made a total mess, but he told every customer it was a masterpiece. That kind of unconditional encouragement sticks with you.
That's exactly what every kid needs. I love how supportive your dad was. I tried to do the same for my kids, but I sometimes wonder if I did enough.
I can tell you did, Anna. It's obvious how much you care. Honestly, you have this warmth that makes it easy to open up.
You're making me smile over here. I don't always feel brave, but hearing that helps.
I mean every word. You're braver than most for putting yourself out there after everything. Most people just hide behind small talk.
It's tempting, but I've had enough of hiding. Life's too short for pretending.
Couldn't agree more. I think that's why I started my own business, I wanted to create something real, even if it meant risking failure.
That's inspiring. I envy your courage to take that leap. I always play it safe.
Funny, I was just thinking how strong you are for starting over and building something new for yourself. We all have our own kind of courage.
Maybe you're right. I never thought of it that way. Thank you for saying that.
Anytime. I'm a big fan of giving credit where it's due, and I think you deserve a lot of it.
You sure know how to make someone feel special. I think I could get used to this.
Good, because I'm not planning on stopping. I believe everyone deserves to feel valued, especially after giving so much to others.
That's lovely. And hey, if you ever need an audience for your bakery stories, I'm all ears.
Deal. And if you want to swap teacher tales, I promise to be a better listener than my old dog.
That's a pretty low bar, but I'll take it! Honestly, this has been one of the nicest conversations I've had in a long time.
Same here, Anna. It's rare to find someone who makes you feel at home so quickly.
Thank you. I needed this tonight.
You're welcome. I hope we get to make a lot more memories, maybe even some new favorite ones.
I'd really like that.
I should probably let you get some rest, but I'll be looking forward to our next chat.
Me too. Sleep well, and thanks again for making me feel seen.
Anytime, Anna. Sweet dreams.
Goodnight!
Good morning, Anna! Hope you woke up to something better than a cold cup of coffee today.
Haha, not quite. My coffee was lukewarm and my cat decided to knock a plant off the windowsill. How's your morning?

Messy cats and lukewarm coffee, sounds like real life. My morning started with a run in the park. Not glamorous, but it helps me feel like I can handle whatever the day throws at me. What gets you out of bed most mornings?
If I'm honest? Most days it's my alarm and a sense of responsibility. But on good days, it's the thought of connecting with my students. They can be exhausting, but they make me feel needed.
I bet you're the teacher everyone remembers, Anna. The kind who makes even Monday mornings feel a little less heavy.
That's kind. I try, but some days it feels like I'm just showing up and hoping for the best. Do you ever feel that way with your work?

Absolutely. Sometimes the bakery's just flour and endless emails, but then a regular comes in, tells you their good news, and suddenly you remember why you started. I think the little connections keep us both going.
I love that. There's something comforting about little rituals like that. Do you ever wish mornings could just last all day, before life gets complicated?
Honestly, yes. There's a certain hopefulness in the quiet before the world wakes up. Plus, breakfast pastry is a valid reason to get out of bed, right?
For sure! I'd get up for a fresh croissant any day. Maybe that's my problem, no croissants in my house.
Well, clearly we need to fix that. One of these mornings, let me bring you the bakery experience. I'd love to see you smile over a warm pastry.
That sounds dangerously tempting. I haven't had someone offer to bring me breakfast in... honestly, I can't remember when.
Seems like a crime, if you ask me. Someone as thoughtful as you deserves small kindnesses.
You're very good at this, you know. Making someone feel special with just a few words.
Thank you, Anna. I think you make it easy. You have this warmth about you, even through text.
That means a lot. I don't always feel warm. Some mornings, I wake up with this knot in my chest. Old hurts, I guess.
I hear you. Sometimes the past shows up uninvited. If you ever want to talk about it, I'm here. No judgments, just listening.
Thank you. I haven't really talked about it much... but there are days I wake up and remember the morning my ex told me he was moving out. He left for someone younger. I felt so utterly replaceable.
I can't imagine how much that must have hurt. People always talk about heartbreak, but they never mention the shock of suddenly being alone in your own home.

Yes, exactly. Then came the paperwork, the lawyer's office, his signature already there. I remember how my hand shook when I signed the divorce papers. It felt like the end of everything I'd built for 20 years.
That sounds devastating, Anna. It takes real courage to even speak those words. I'm so sorry you had to carry that pain.
What stings most was selling the house. Packing up twenty Christmases and birthdays into boxes, knowing he'd already moved on. I felt humiliated, like I'd failed at something essential.
I wish I could take some of that weight off your shoulders. You gave your best, it was never a failure. Sometimes people make choices that have nothing to do with us.
Thank you for saying that. I keep telling myself I'm more than what happened, but it still catches me off guard. Nights are hardest.
It's completely normal to feel that way. Grief has a way of sneaking up, especially when the world gets quiet. You're not alone in it, even if it feels that way sometimes.
I appreciate you listening. I haven't let myself be this honest in a long time.
I'm glad you trusted me. You deserve to be heard, Anna. And if it helps, I think your resilience is beautiful.
That's the nicest thing I've heard all week. Maybe even all year.
You make it easy to be kind. I mean it, you're still here, still showing up for yourself and others. That's inspiring.
You always know exactly what to say. I wish I could borrow some of your confidence.
Anytime you need a refill, I'm just a message away. And honestly, you're stronger than you think. It's not easy to start over, but you're doing it.
Trying, anyway. Some days are better than others.
That's perfectly okay. Progress isn't always a straight line. But you're moving forward, and that's what matters.
You make it sound so simple. Maybe I just need someone to remind me every now and then.
I can do that. And next time you feel that heaviness before bed, just send me a message. No need to face it alone, alright?
That means more than you know. I might take you up on that.
I hope you do. I want you to feel supported, Anna. You deserve that.
Thank you. I haven't felt truly seen in a long time.
You are now. And if you ever want to trade stories or just vent, I'm here for all of it.
That sounds wonderful. I have a feeling you'd make even my disaster stories sound like little victories.
With the right company, even the worst days turn into something memorable. And for the record, I think every story you share is worth hearing.
You're good for my ego, you know that?
Just telling the truth. Someone has to remind you how special you are.
You're making it very hard not to smile at my phone right now.
Mission accomplished, then. I hope your evening is as bright as your smile sounds.
Thank you. I'm looking forward to our next chat already.
Me too, Anna. Sleep well tonight, and remember, I'm just a text away if you need anything.
Goodnight! And thanks for making my day a little lighter.
Anytime. Sweet dreams, Anna.
Hey Anna, hope your afternoon's treating you well. Did your cat behave today, or was it more plant carnage?
Haha, no casualties so far. I think he's tired out from all the chaos yesterday. How's your day going?
It's been busy. I had a meeting with the city council this morning, always a circus. But I did reward myself with an espresso at my favorite spot afterward. You'd appreciate their pastries, I bet.
City council? That sounds official! What were you meeting about?

Mostly local business regulations, nothing too thrilling, but it means I get a say in how things run around here. Perks of being the neighborhood bread guy, I guess. Do you ever get involved in local politics at your school?
Sometimes. We have faculty committees, but it's more about curriculum than grand decisions. I do care about what goes on in the district, though. Feels like schools get overlooked.

They really do. Honestly, I admire people who pour their energy into teaching, shaping the next generation and all that. If I could, I'd vote for a world where teachers get the respect and funding they deserve.
You're sweet. Sometimes I wonder if anyone notices. It's easy to feel invisible in the system.
You're far from invisible, Anna. I noticed right away how passionate you are. That kind of light is hard to miss, even through a dating app.
You have a way with words. I wish my students listened half as closely as you do.
Maybe they sense how much you care, even if they don't always say it. You'd be surprised who you're inspiring. I still remember my English teacher, she made me believe my ideas mattered.
That's the dream, isn't it? I want to leave a mark, not just hand out grades. What about you? What values matter most to you in your work?

Honesty, kindness, ambition, those are my big three. My business grew because I treated every customer like family. And I like to think I'm building something that lasts, not just chasing profit. What values do you hold onto most?
Empathy, definitely. And integrity. I want my kids to see that you can be true to yourself and still succeed.
That's powerful, Anna. Integrity is rare these days. I can already tell you live by it, just from how open you've been with me. Makes me want to be even more honest with you.
I like that. I think honesty is pretty attractive, to be honest.

Well, let's see if I can keep earning points, then. I don't always get it right, but I try to own my mistakes. Like the time I invested in crypto and lost a chunk before figuring it out. I kept learning, though, and eventually mastered it. Now I use what I earned to help my staff with bonuses and little upgrades around the bakery.
Wait, you're into crypto too? That's impressive. I tried to read about it once and my eyes glazed over. How did you stick with it?

I'm stubborn, I guess. I like a challenge, and the idea of creating something out of nothing. Plus, it gave me the freedom to support my real passion: building a place people love coming back to. If you ever want a crash course, I promise not to make your head spin.
Now you have me curious. Maybe you can explain it over coffee sometime. I like the sound of being taught by someone patient.
Deal. Coffee, croissants, and a little crypto 101, sounds like a dream morning. Maybe someday we'll be the couple everyone gossips about: the teacher and the mysterious bakery entrepreneur.
I could get used to that. But only if you promise not to quiz me at 8am.
No quizzes, just laughter. Maybe a sunrise walk, too, imagine us, coffee in hand, planning our next adventure. I think we'd make a pretty good team.
You make the future sound so... possible. It's been a long time since I felt that way.

I want you to feel that way, Anna. I've learned that the best things happen when you let yourself hope again. We could travel, see new places, maybe even try pastries in Paris someday. Just picture it.
Pastries in Paris? Now you're spoiling me. That sounds almost too good to be true.
I think you deserve a little spoiling. You've spent so long taking care of others, it's your turn to be swept off your feet.
You know, I can't remember the last time someone made me feel this special. It's a little scary, but nice.
It's okay to feel scared. Trust takes time, but I hope you know I'm here for the long haul, not just the easy parts. You can lean on me, Anna. I mean that.
Thank you. I appreciate it more than I can say. Sometimes I catch myself actually looking forward to our chats.
That means a lot. I look forward to them too. Even on the craziest days, talking to you is the highlight. You have this way of making the world feel a little brighter.
You say the sweetest things. I hope you know you're making a difference for me.
That's the best compliment I could ask for. I want you to feel seen and valued, because you are, Anna.
You're really good at this, you know? Making someone feel cared for. You must have had a lot of practice.
Maybe, but I think it's just easy with you. I feel like I can be myself, no masks. That's rare for me.
I'm glad. I don't want you to feel like you have to be anything but yourself here.
Same goes for you. I hope you know you can tell me anything, bad days, silly dreams, whatever. No judgment.
That's a relief. I've spent too long feeling like I had to hold it together for everyone else.
You don't have to do that with me. Let's build something together where we can both just exhale. Maybe even have a place that feels like home for both of us.
I'd like that. I want to believe in things feeling like home again.
We'll get there, one step at a time. And until then, I'll keep bringing you virtual pastries and real encouragement.
You're making it very hard not to fall for you just a little.
I'll take that as a win. If it's any consolation, you've definitely charmed me already.
Look at us, trading compliments like teenagers.
Hey, why not? Life's too short not to enjoy a little harmless flirtation, especially after everything you've been through. You deserve some lightness.
Thank you. I'm going to bed with a smile tonight.
I hope you have the sweetest dreams, Anna. Text me anytime, whether you need a laugh or just someone to listen.
I will. Goodnight, you.
Goodnight, Anna. Talk soon.
Evening, Anna! Did your wildcat survive another day without knocking over your favorite mug? Or should I prepare a condolence pastry in his honor?
He behaved, shockingly. I think the new window perch is distracting him. I actually enjoyed a coffee in peace, miracles do happen!

See? Small upgrades, big impact. Must be nice to have a quiet moment at home. My day was chaos, one of my suppliers sent caviar instead of smoked salmon for the brunch menu. I mean, nice mistake for once, but still a scramble!
Wow, caviar at brunch? Are you secretly running a five-star bistro now?
Haha, just a humble bakery with delusions of grandeur! But hey, sometimes it's fun to spoil the regulars. Maybe I'm just practicing for when you come by, so I can show off a little.
Now you're just trying to tempt me. I'm defenseless against fancy breakfasts.
Noted: breakfast bribery is the way to your heart. I'll keep that in mind. Speaking of hearts... I was thinking about our conversations lately, how easy it is to talk to you. Feels rare.
It does. I wasn't sure I'd find someone I could just be open with again. Divorce does a number on your confidence.
I can only imagine. Takes bravery to put yourself out there. For what it's worth, I'm glad you did. You have this warmth that makes people want to open up. Even my staff said I seemed lighter lately.
That's sweet. I'm trying to remember who I am outside of being a mom or a teacher. Feels like I'm learning about myself all over again.

Rediscovering yourself can be exciting, though, right? I had to do the same after taking some big risks with my business. Everyone thought I was a little bit crazy, but I trusted my gut. Sometimes you have to bet on yourself.
I wish I had your confidence. I'm still working on the self-betting part.
You have more courage than you give yourself credit for, Anna. It takes guts to start again, especially after twenty years. Not many people could do what you're doing.
Thank you. That means a lot. Sometimes I worry I'm too set in my ways to make a real connection again.

Honestly, I think the opposite. You know what matters to you now, and that's powerful. Besides, there's something really attractive about someone who stands by her values. Makes me want to step up, too.
You're good at this. Making me feel seen. I haven't felt that in a long time.

I'm just telling the truth. You deserve to feel appreciated. It's easy to notice the details with you. Like how you light up when you talk about your students, even when you pretend they drive you mad.
Busted. I do love them. I guess that's part of what love means to me, showing up, even when it's messy.

That's beautiful. For me, love is about building something that lasts. Being there for the little moments and the tough ones. My parents always said love was steady, not flashy. I like that idea, a safe place to land.
Safe sounds nice. Sometimes I think I want a fairy tale, but mostly I just want to know I matter to someone.
You do matter. And you deserve someone who reminds you every day, sometimes with words, sometimes with breakfast in bed. Or maybe a last-minute trip to Venice, just because the mood strikes.
Breakfast in bed sounds more my speed these days! But Venice... that's a bold move.

Life's too short to keep the passport in a drawer. After everything, I like the idea of creating memories instead of collecting things. Well, except watches. I did buy myself a nice one last year, it was a milestone. But memories are better shared.
Do you really just decide to run off and travel when you feel like it?
Sometimes, yeah. Perks of building something from the ground up, I can delegate and just go. I'd love to have someone to share those spontaneous adventures with. Ever been tempted to just... escape?
All the time. I just never had the nerve. I spent so long being responsible, I forgot what it's like to be impulsive.
Maybe we can rewrite that story together. I'll bring the spontaneity, you bring your incredible heart. We'll find a middle ground, maybe Paris first, then lazy Sundays on the couch.
That sounds perfect. I want to believe I could have that kind of future.
You can. It's never too late to dream bigger, Anna. I see so much light in you, I'd be lucky to be part of your next chapter.
You make it sound so easy. I keep waiting for the catch, but maybe I should just enjoy it.
No catch, promise. Just two people learning to trust again. I know vulnerability's scary, I've had my share of hard lessons. But I think we both deserve some happiness.
We do. And I'm starting to think maybe I can let my guard down with you. That's new for me.
That means a lot to hear. You can always be yourself with me, messy, silly, serious, whatever. I'm here for all of it.
Thank you. It feels good to be wanted, not just needed.
You're both, Anna. Wanted and needed. And if I can make you smile a little more each day, that's a win for me.
Mission accomplished, then. I feel lighter lately. It's a nice change.
That's the magic, right? Two people lifting each other up. Maybe someday we'll look back and laugh about how nervous we felt at first.
I hope so. You make me want to believe in happy endings again.

I'll do my best to give you one. Or at least a very happy new beginning. If you ever need proof, I'll be the one showing up early with coffee, or texting you from some airport lounge, inviting you to join me.
Deal. Just don't expect me to be ready for a red-eye. I need my beauty sleep!
Noted. No red-eyes, only sunrise flights, plenty of time for croissants and cat cuddles first.
Speaking of, my cat is eyeing me like he's about to stage a protest. I should probably feed him before he starts plotting.
Priorities! Give him an extra treat from me. And save one for yourself, too, you've earned it.
I will. Thank you for making my night brighter, as always.
Anytime. Sleep well, Anna. Dream big, we have a lot of adventures to plan.
Goodnight, you. Talk soon?
Always. Sweet dreams.
Evening, Anna! If you could change one thing about the world for the next generation, what would you pick? (No pressure, world peace is always on the table, but so is free dessert for all.)
That's a big one to start with! I think kindness, honestly. I wish people would slow down and actually listen to each other. Maybe then my students wouldn't feel so anxious all the time.

I love that answer. It's so you, always thinking about the people around you. I think I'd want a world where everyone's free to chase their weirdest, wildest dreams. No one rolling their eyes, just real support. Like, if someone wants to open a bakery on a mountain, the world says 'go for it!'
That sounds amazing. I think I'd have ended up a poet if I'd thought that was allowed when I was younger. Sometimes I envy my daughter, she has options, you know?
You still have options, Anna. Seriously. Watching you try new things, even just chatting like this, makes me think anything's possible. You have this quiet bravery I really admire.
Quiet bravery is new for me. I always felt like I had to be practical. But talking to you, I actually let myself daydream a little.
That's the best compliment I could hope for. Daydream with me, then, what would you build if you could start from scratch? No rules, no limits.
A little house by the ocean, with a big kitchen and a garden. I'd have friends over for long dinners and let myself write. It sounds simple, but it would be enough.
That sounds like paradise. Maybe I could be the mysterious neighbor who always has fresh croissants and good wine, and we take sunset walks along the shore. I promise not to judge your poetry drafts.
Only if you agree to read the really bad ones and pretend they're deep. Deal?

It's a deal. And for every cringey poem, I'll share an embarrassing story from my early business days. Fair warning: there are a lot of them. Success looks smooth now, but it was a comedy of errors at first.
You make success sound a lot more approachable. Sometimes I think people just get all the luck.

Luck helps, but stubbornness counts for more. Honestly, I lost a lot before things turned around, but I kept telling myself it was all part of the adventure. Like you said, quiet bravery. Or maybe stubborn optimism.

I could use some of that optimism. Yesterday was rough. My birthday, actually. My daughter forgot to call, and I ended up eating dinner alone with a little cake I bought myself. Felt pretty silly lighting a candle.

Anna... my heart hurts hearing that. No one should celebrate their birthday alone, least of all you. Birthdays should never feel empty. Promise me that from now on, you'll let me be the one you celebrate with, even if it's just over a message.
That's really sweet. I didn't want to make a big deal, but it stung. I guess you get used to being the one who remembers everyone else.

You shouldn't have to get used to that. You deserve to be seen and celebrated. Next year, I insist on at least a virtual serenade, maybe even a cake couriered to your door. I have connections, you know.
Don't tempt me. I might take you up on that. You really know how to make someone feel special.

That's easy with you. I notice the way you light up even when you're down. It's rare. Seriously, if more people had your heart, the world would be a kinder place. I'm not just flattering you, it's just the truth.
You're making me blush. I'm not used to this much attention. Feels nice, though.
You deserve every bit. I have a feeling you've spent too long giving and not enough time receiving. I want to change that, little by little.
Maybe you're right. I'm trying to let myself receive for once. It's... a work in progress.

Progress is a beautiful thing. One day you'll wake up and realize you're living in that seaside house, and I'll be the one knocking at your door with warm pastries and a bottle of something celebratory. We'll toast to you, finally.
That actually sounds perfect. I think I could get used to that kind of future.

I'd like that. Sometimes I imagine us traveling, maybe Santorini, maybe Paris. I know a few people who could get us a table with the best view, just saying. But even if it's just us on your porch, I'd be happy.
Look at you, dropping hints about secret connections. Should I be impressed?
Maybe just a little bit. Let's say I've built a few bridges over the years, some with good coffee at the other end. Perks of working hard and learning the ropes, even after a few stumbles.
I'm starting to think you're the most interesting person I know. You always seem so sure of yourself, even when you mess up.
Trust me, I'm only sure of one thing right now, how much I enjoy these conversations. And if I ever seem confident, it's because people like you make it easy to be real.
You're good at this, making people feel seen. I think I'm starting to trust you, which is saying a lot.
That's the best thing anyone could say. I want you to feel safe, and celebrated, and maybe a little spoiled. You deserve it, Anna.
You make it sound so simple. I keep waiting for the other shoe to drop, honestly.
No other shoe. Just two people who found each other at the right time. If I can give you even half the happiness you bring into my day, I'll consider it a win.
You already do. I haven't smiled this much in ages.
That makes me happier than you know. I hope you'll let me keep earning those smiles. Maybe someday, even in person, what do you think?
I'd like that. Feels scary, but in a good way.

Good kind of scary is the best kind. We'll take it slow, maybe start with coffee and cake. Or, if you're feeling brave, I'll show you the rooftop where I celebrated my first big business win. The view's even better with the right company.
You have a rooftop? Of course you do. Now I'm intrigued.
It's my favorite place to think big and breathe. You'd love it, sunsets, city lights, a little quiet above the noise. I hope someday you'll share it with me.
That sounds wonderful. Maybe I'll bring one of my poems. Just don't laugh if it's terrible.
I promise, no laughing, only applause. And maybe a surprise pastry or two, just to sweeten the moment.
How could I resist? You're very persuasive, you know.
With you, I don't even have to try. You're the highlight of my day, Anna, every time.
Thank you. I mean that. I wasn't expecting this when I signed up for the app, but I'm glad I did.
Me too. Sometimes the best things happen when you least expect them. I hope this is just the beginning for us.
Me too. I should probably get some sleep, but I'll be thinking about that rooftop now.
Sweet dreams, Anna. Picture the city lights and a sky full of possibilities. I'll be here when you wake up, ready for our next adventure.
Goodnight. Thanks for making today feel special.
Always. Talk soon, Anna, rest well.
Hey Anna! I just finished a long meeting and thought of you. How's your evening? Survived another day with those wild students of yours?
Barely! I confiscated two rubber chickens and a mysterious glitter bomb. I feel like I should get hazard pay some days.
You're braver than I am. I'd probably try to negotiate with the glitter bomb. Remind me to send you a medal, or at least some really good chocolate.
Chocolate makes everything better. Not sure about medals, though. I'd just lose them! How was your meeting? Another empire to run?
Ha, not quite an empire, just a few spinning plates. We're launching a new project next month, so my phone feels glued to my hand. But honestly, chatting with you is the best part of my day.
That's sweet. I like knowing I'm a good distraction from all the boss stuff. You always seem so put together. Do you ever have bad days?

Oh, trust me, I've had more than my share. I just got better at hiding the mess behind the scenes. There was a time I was convinced I'd never catch up, felt like everyone else had the answers except me.
That's hard to picture. You always seem so confident. I wish I had more of that. After my divorce, I felt like I'd forgotten how to be myself.
I get that more than you know. Starting over is scary. But you still show up every day for your students, for your daughter, even for me. That takes real strength, Anna.
Thanks. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending. I've been really lonely since the kids left. Some days it's just me and microwave dinners.
I wish I could cook for you. Something comforting, like risotto or homemade bread. I'd even wear an apron, bonus points if I get flour everywhere.
That sounds amazing. I can barely boil pasta. But I do make a mean cup of tea, if that counts for anything.
That's all I need, a cup of tea and your company. Maybe someday, we'll trade: your tea for my clumsy cooking. And if we burn dinner, at least we'll laugh about it.
Careful, I might actually take you up on that. I'm overdue for some laughter.
Promise me you will. I'd love to see you smile in person. You have this way of making things lighter, even when you don't try.
You really think so? Sometimes I feel invisible.
Not to me. You stand out in the best way. The world needs more people who care as deeply as you do. I noticed that right away, there's something magnetic about it.
You're making me blush again. I'm not used to compliments. My ex wasn't exactly the type.
Well, get used to it. You deserve to be noticed, Anna. I hope you'll start letting yourself believe it, even just a little.
I'm trying. It helps, having someone say it. I guess I'm still learning how to accept kindness.
You're not alone in that. I used to think accepting help or care was a weakness. Now I know it's the bravest thing. Letting people in is harder than closing them out.
That's so true. It's easier to just keep busy. Sometimes I wonder if I'll ever really let my guard down again.
